findings.text: clear() resolves the governing lift with session=None, and _applies refuses every session-scoped lift when session is None, so a session-scoped lift can never be revoked: with only a session lift recorded clear() returns None, and with a global lift present too it revokes the global one and leaves the session lift in force. Reproduced: granting a global (1.5) and a session ('s1', 1.8) lift then clear(group) returned the global lift's id, and effective_budget(session='s1') still returned the lifted block. The plan's '--clear --group <group> revokes one' provides no session targeting, so the CLI follow-on inherits this.

effective_budget sets the returned block's pace_multiple to None for the drain-by and uncapped forms (float(lift['pace_multiple']) only when form==multiple), so a wiring reader that reads block['pace_multiple'] the way pace.allowance_for_group does gets None for those forms; the form is recoverable from block['pace_hold'] and block['lift'], but the None is a landmine for the reader the plan says reads it for the multiple.

the plan requires that budget.lift.max_multiple and budget.lift.max_hours be writable in a flight layer and accepted by the schema, but BudgetConfig forbids extra keys and no budget.lift slot was declared (flight.yaml is outside this node's declared write paths); ceilings() therefore reads config['budget']['lift'], a key the current schema rejects, so the config-driven ceilings are unreachable until the slot lands.

the max_multiple-from-config path is untested — test_grant_refuses_a_multiple_above_the_declared_ceiling exercises only the shipped default (bl.DEFAULT_MAX_MULTIPLE), while the plan's 'a lift at 2.5 is refused under a layer setting max_multiple to 2' has no test that supplies max_multiple through config as test_max_hours_bounds_a_lift_whose_reset_never_moves does for max_hours.

the manifest's own follow_ons names the remainder of §10 — the CLI surface, the wiring of the three readers (pace.allowance_for_group, reserve.admit_windows, budget.decide via budget.policy), pace_hold.releases_at, pace.lift_id on dispatch rows, the follower transition lines, the reckon-build skill fence and the help-contract tests — so a granted lift changes no dispatch decision end to end; the resolver is delivered pure and ready for a caller.

The two pre-existing files ran identically at head: 35 passed (they are unchanged between base and head — the diff touches neither — so this is the base arm's result), giving 23 new tests, all green, and zero added failures. Negative control reproduced independently: applying the declared mutation (effective_budget returns config["budget"] unchanged) in a scratch copy reddened exactly 5 tests, exit 1 — test_effective_budget_returns_the_lifted_block_with_reserves_released (which carries both the 1.8-admit assertion and the role_ceiling_pct==100 assertion), test_max_hours_bounds_a_lift_whose_reset_never_moves, test_an_uncapped_lift_marks_no_pace_hold, and the two session-scope tests — matching the reviewed log. The plan's reset-anchored end conditions are each covered (moved resets_at, utilisation below the grant figure, a fall between two readings, past-at, cleared, past max_hours, future from). Bullets NOT met by this node: the three readers' wiring, the budget.lift.max_multiple/max_hours schema slot, the CLI, releases_at, lift_id on rows, follower lines, skill fence and help-contract tests — all named in follow_ons.
VERDICT write_paths: git diff baca1446c..181f998c0 lists exactly three paths — reckon/crew/budget_lift.py, tests/test_budget_lift.py, docs/evidence/fragments/a-window-paces-the-lane/a-lift-resolves-the-effective-budget.html — all inside the node's declared write paths. VERDICT diff: Read line by line. effective_budget substitutes a copied budget block; _governing_lift selects by group, scope and in-force; _in_force checks cleared/start/max_hours/stated-end/reset-observed; _reset_observed implements the three-signal reset detection (moved stamp, utilisation below the grant figure, and a fall between two consecutive readings above the floor); grant refuses an undeclared group, a multiple at or below the configured one, one above the ceiling, a missing reason, and a fenced run.
